discovery: Electromagnetic metamaterials: negative refraction, the perfect lens and transformation optics
motivation: Pendry showed that sub-wavelength structured media (wire arrays, split-ring resonators) could be designed to have effective permittivity and permeability not found in nature, and predicted that a negative-index slab acts as a 'perfect lens' amplifying evanescent waves beyond the diffraction limit. Smith and coworkers realised the first negative-index metamaterial and verified negative refraction experimentally (2000-2001). Pendry and Smith then founded transformation optics, demonstrating the first electromagnetic cloak in 2006. Together they turned the constitutive parameters of matter into engineerable design variables. This idea now underpins hyperbolic media, metasurfaces, flat optics, superlenses, and coherent control of metamaterial resonances, and it has spread to acoustics, thermal transport and seismics. It is a conceptual discovery about light-matter interaction that became a practical control knob used by physicists and engineers worldwide.
